These are two separate requests because they answer different questions.

## 1. Phone screenshot: what the user actually sees

**Goal:** Show the design as a real person sees it when the page loads on a phone.

- **Viewport:** Use a common phone size, such as 390×844 CSS pixels (a modern iPhone) or 360×800 (a typical Android).
- **Pixel density:** Use a device scale factor of 2× or 3× so text and icons look crisp, like they do on a real high-DPI screen.
- **Mobile emulation:** Use a mobile user agent and touch emulation. This makes responsive breakpoints, mobile-only layouts, and hover-free states render correctly.
- **Capture area:** Capture only the visible viewport, the area "above the fold." Don't capture the whole page. What matters is the first impression on one screen.
- **State:** Wait until fonts, images, and animations have settled. Decide whether to include or dismiss overlays like cookie banners, depending on what the designer wants to judge.
- **Output:** One image at true phone proportions, suitable for mockups or a device frame.

## 2. Full-height component review: the whole element, top to bottom

**Goal:** Let the designer check the entire long component, including spacing, alignment, and consistency, without scrolling through many screenshots.

- **Target:** Capture the component itself, not the page or the viewport. Picking it by selector crops away unrelated page content.
- **Height:** Capture its full rendered height, even far beyond the viewport, so the image runs from its first pixel to its last.
- **Width:** Use the width the component is being reviewed at, either the same phone width (for a mobile review) or a desktop width. Keep it consistent so measurements line up.
- **Lazy content:** Scroll through or trigger lazy-loaded images and deferred sections before capturing. Otherwise the lower parts may show blanks or placeholders.
- **Sticky and fixed elements:** Hide or neutralize sticky headers and floating buttons. In a tall capture they can be drawn over the middle of the component or repeated.
- **Output:** One tall image, sized for close inspection and annotation rather than for display on a device.

## The core distinction

| | Phone screenshot | Component review |
|---|---|---|
| Question answered | "What does the user see?" | "Is every part of this built right?" |
| Scope | Viewport only | One element, full height |
| Fidelity priority | Real device conditions | Completeness of content |
| Typical use | Presentations, UX validation | Design QA, redlines, spacing checks |

Keeping them as separate requests prevents a common mistake: a full-page capture misrepresents what the user sees on a phone, and a viewport capture hides most of a long component.

type ScreenId  = string & { readonly __brand: "ScreenId" };

  screenId: ScreenId;
  changes: ScreenChanges;
}
